title: Isolation of murine hepatic myeloid cells with high yield and purity using immunomagnetic beads for subset analysis
protocol: Freshly and aseptically prepare all buffers and reagents for liver digestion in a laminar hood.
Pre-warm the PB and DB to 38°C in the water bath before use.
Measure the temperature of the outflow using another thermometer before starting the perfusion step.
Place the inlet tubing into a 50 mL tube containing 40 mL PB in a 38°C water bath.
Set up the pump speed at 5 mL/min.
Ensure that the surgical table or surface is clean and sterile with 75% ethanol.
Cover the entire polystyrene foam pad with a sheet of aluminum foil to create a disposable dissection board.
Place the dissection board near the perfusion pump inside a waste fluid collection container.
Assemble the outlet tubing with a 26G needle.
Flush the outlet tubing with 10 mL of 70% ethanol.
Flush the outlet tubing with 10 mL of 1× PBS.
Run the pump with PB for 3 min to ensure a stable flow rate.
Remove air bubbles from the perfusion system and catheter.
Measure body weight of the mouse.
Anesthetize the mouse by inhalation of isoflurane (4% in oxygen).
Administer ketamine (60 mg/kg) and xylazine (12 mg/kg) in normal saline by intraperitoneal injection.
Ensure that the animal is adequately anesthetized and exhibits regular breathing.
Use an electric clipper to remove fur on the entire abdomen and lower thorax of the animal.
Position the mouse ventral side up on a clean dissection board.
Secure the mouse’s limbs with locking pins or medical adhesive tapes.
Clean the anterior abdomen using sterile cotton swabs first with 75% alcohol, followed by iodine.
Make a longitudinal midline incision on the ventral abdomen approximately 1–2 cm above the hind legs.
Create a transverse incision along the lower rib cage and ensure integrity of the diaphragm wall.
Gently displace the intestine to the side of the mouse’s body to expose the liver.
Start the perfusion pump and set the perfusion rate at 5 mL/min.
Insert a 26G catheter into the portal vein that has already been connected to the perfusion system.
Clamp the portal vein tightly to secure the catheter.
Insert a catheter with a syringe of 26-gauge into the portal vein.
Constrict the portal vein securely with a vascular clamp to prevent dislodging of the catheter.
Cut through the diaphragm to expose the thoracic cavity.
Clamp the proximal portion of the IVC to ensure blood supply to the liver in situ.
Compress the distal portion of the IVC for 7–10 seconds using forceps to avoid fluid leakage from the liver.
Observe a transition from reddish-brown to light brown as an indicator of good liver condition.
Digest the liver tissue until it lacks distinct shape, texture, and organization, appearing more amorphous and disrupted.
Remove the whole liver from the animal and place it on a cell strainer with 70 μm mesh width on top of a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Clamp the proximal part of IVC to maximize in situ liver perfusion efficiency.
Clamp the distal part of IVC for 7-10 seconds to prevent fluid exit from the liver.
Release the clamp to allow fluid to exit.
Repeat the clamping and releasing procedure 4-5 times.
Continue perfusing with PB for an additional 5 minutes after the liver appears enlarged and light brown.
Displace the inlet tubing from the PB tube to a 50 mL tube containing 40 mL of DB in a 38°C water bath.
Stop the pump temporarily before displacing the tubing.
Maintain a constant flow rate of 5 mL/min for 5 min during displacement.
Remove the entire liver from the animal without cutting or puncturing the gut.
Place the liver in a cell strainer with 70 μm mesh on top of a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Keep the tube on ice throughout the process.
Add HBSS buffer intermittently to the strainer.
Gently swirl the liver within HBSS+ buffer using a pipette tip or dropper tip to facilitate dissociation of liver cells.
Repeat the procedure until the final volume of the filtered cell suspension reaches 50 mL.
Perform all procedures on ice.
Optimize the exact time for liver digestion using 0.5% collagenase to avoid over-digestion or under-digestion.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 4°C for 5 min at 50 × g in a swing-out rotor.
Transfer the supernatant containing mainly non-parenchyma cells (NPCs) to a clean tube.
Discard the pellet containing mostly parenchymal cells (PCs).
Repeat centrifugation of the recovered supernatant at 4°C for 5 min at 50 × g to remove residual PCs.
Transfer the supernatant to a clean 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge NPCs at 300 × g (1260 rpm) for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and keep the NPC cell pellet on ice.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of 1× RBC lysis buffer and incubate at 20°C–24°C for 1 min to lyse red blood cells.
Add 9 mL of 1× PBS to a final volume of 10 mL and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of HBSS+.
Mix an aliquot of 10 μL isolated NPC suspension with 90 μL of 0.4% trypan blue solution by gently pipetting.
Count the cell number and assess the viability of the isolated cells from a 10 μL aliquot of the mixture using a cell counter or hemocytometer.
Transfer the NPC suspension to a sterilized flow cytometry tube.
Centrifuge the NPCs at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the NPC pellets in 100 μL of cell-staining buffer at a density of 1 × 10^8 cells/mL.
Add 1 μL of BD Mouse Fc Block to the NPCs and incubate for 10 minutes on ice.
Add 3 μL of APC-labeled anti-CD45 antibody to the Fc block-treated cells.
Incubate on ice for another 30 min.
Protect from light.
Thoroughly mix the BD IMag Anti-APC Magnetic Particles.
Aliquot 50 μL of the beads to the cells sample, resulting in a total volume of 150 μL.
Incubate the tube on ice for 30 min.
Place the tube-containing BD IMag-labeled cell suspension onto a Cell Separation Magnet (e.g., BD IMagnet).
Allow the magnetic beads-bound cells to accumulate at the tube wall for 6–8 min.
Remove and discard the depleted supernatant carefully.
Wash the magnetic bead-bound cells by suspending them in 1 mL of 1× BD IMag buffer.
Gently pipette the cells up and down.
Reposit the tube to the Cell Separation Magnet for another 2–4 min.
Repeat the washing step once.
Resuspend the magnetic bead-bound cells with 1 mL of 1× PBS after the final wash.
Count the number and check the viability of CD45+ cells by a cell counter or a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the magnetic bead-bound cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the magnetic bead-bound cell pellets in 100 μL cell-staining buffer.
Add all the fluorophore-labeled specific antibodies of interest at a ratio of 1:100 to the resuspended cells and mix well.
Add the isotype control at the same concentration as the specific antibody.
Prepare an antibody mixture by combining all antibodies of interest in a single tube.
Adjust the final volume of the antibody mixture to 100 μL with cell-staining buffer.
Resuspend magnetic bead pellets with the antibody mixture.
Mix the antibodies thoroughly with the cells and incubate on ice for 30 min in the dark.
Wash the cells by adding 3 mL of 1× PBS to each sample tube.
Centrifuge at 300 × g (1260 rpm) for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and repeat this wash step twice more.
After the final wash, resuspend the cell pellets in 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Add 1 μL of a cell-impermeable DNA dye to stain dead cells.
Incubate the mixture for 10–15 min at 20°C–24°C protected from light.
Wash cells twice with 3 mL of 1× PBS, decant the supernatant and gently mix to loosen the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellets in 200 μL of 1× PBS for flow cytometry analysis.
Perform the flow cytometric analysis using a flow cytometer.
If isolation of specific myeloid subsets by FACS is desired, use an alternative sorting instrument such as the BD FACSAria III Sorter.
Conduct cell analysis on FlowJo software.
Use an 85 μm nozzle and set the flow rate to 1.5 for optimal sorting results.
Set voltages for each stain using unstained and single-stain controls.
Exclude cell fragments and multicellular aggregates from analysis.
Include only FSC singlets, SSC singlets, live (FVS780-negative) cells, and CD45+ (APC-positive) cells in the analysis.
Analyze subsets of CD45+ myeloid cells including Kupffer cells (KCs) and Ly6C+ monocytes.
Perform a single wash with PBS 2 h after plating to eliminate dead cells and MoMs.
Culture remaining attached cells for 24 h to achieve a mature macrophage phenotype.
Stain sorted resident macrophages with anti-F4/80 (green) and the Hoechst dye (blue).
Rerun an aliquot of the sorted fractions through the Flow cytometer to assess purity.
Cytospin sorted cells onto a slide using a Cytospin 4 centrifuge for further staining.
